You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order with their section headings removed. File every sentence under one of these four headings: SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE EXAM, OBJECTIVE RESULTS, ASSESSMENT AND PLAN. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

SECTION DEFINITIONS
- SUBJECTIVE: what the patient reports and the history taken before the examination: the reason for the visit, the history of the present illness, the review of systems, past medical, surgical, family and social history, current medications and allergies.
- OBJECTIVE EXAM: what the clinician found on physical examination at this visit, including vital signs measured at the visit.
- OBJECTIVE RESULTS: results of laboratory tests, imaging and other studies that were reviewed.
- ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: the clinician's diagnoses or impressions, the reasoning behind them, treatment decisions, prescriptions, orders, referrals, patient instructions and follow-up.
A sentence goes under the heading that names its role in the note, not its topic. A symptom the patient reports belongs under SUBJECTIVE even if the plan discusses it again; a sentence that restates a symptom or finding to justify a decision belongs under ASSESSMENT AND PLAN.

<sentences>
S1: He may continue to take Tylenol between the oxycodone doses for any breakthrough pain.
S2: He explains that when he had pain, which has now resolved, it would radiate almost to his groin.
S3: If his symptoms have not improved, we will discuss further treatment options including lithotripsy.
S4: He denies any hematuria.
S5: MSK: Examination of the abdomen: No pain with palpation of the abdomen.
S6: The patient initially thought his pain was due to throwing hay; however, he broke out into a sweat and became nauseated.
S7: The patient should continue to use the strainer when he urinates until the stone passes.
S8: There is no evidence of hydronephrosis.
S9: The CT scan of the abdomen revealed a stone that is measuring 0.5 cm located in the proximal right ureter.
S10: There is CVA tenderness on the right side.
S11: He explains that he has been straining his urine, but has not seen anything.
S12: The patient describes the pain as intermittent after he found out it was a kidney stone.
S13: He denies having kidney stones before, but states that his father has a history of kidney stones in the past.
S14: I have also recommended that we obtain a BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture to evaluate for any signs of infection.
S15: Mason Ward is a pleasant 80-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of kidney stones.
S16: Musculoskeletal: Reports right back pain.
S17: We reviewed the patient's CT results in detail today.
S18: The onset of his pain began 1 week ago when he was in his barn moving hay when he had a sudden onset of right back pain.
S19: I have prescribed the patient oxycodone 5 mg every 6 to 8 hours for pain.
S20: The patient will follow up with me in 1 to 2 weeks to check on his progress.
S21: No rebound or guarding.
S22: I have recommended that we treat the patient conservatively.
S23: The patient was referred from his primary care physician.
S24: He was seen by his primary care physician, who ordered a CT scan and told him that he had a kidney stone.
</sentences>
